privacy.metaDescription: How Contribly handles personal data, GitHub authentication, and account deletion.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: A clear summary of what Contribly does with data. Last updated: August 2026.

sections.title: What we collect
body: GitHub account data used for login (name, email when available, avatar, and username).
Information you fill in your profile (bio, languages, interest tags, level, and invite preference).
Platform activity: published projects, swipes, interests, invites, participations, and match messages.
Public metadata from imported repositories (stars, issues with labels like good first issue / help wanted), synced periodically.

sections.title: What we use it for
body: Authenticating you and keeping your session.
Enabling interest, acceptance, invites, and conversation between contributor and maintainer.
Syncing profile and issues with the GitHub API, when permission or a configured token is available.

sections.title: Where it's stored
body: Authentication via Auth.js with the GitHub OAuth provider.

sections.title: Sharing
body: We do not sell personal data.
Content you publish (projects, accepted interests, match messages) is visible to the parties involved in the product flow.
Infrastructure providers (Vercel, Supabase, GitHub) process data necessary to operate the service.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can edit your profile at any time.
You can delete your account in Profile → Danger zone. This removes your data from Contribly (including projects you published).
The code is open source under the MIT license; audit what the app does in the repository.
